utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, and please remember, slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Groome: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. Sir, I apologise for interrupting you, but there was something I was going to ask you. I was thinking yesterday about the event that happened at Musici, when Milan Lukic came and took away those women, and there's something that's still unclear to me. I have some papers here but they are mixed up. I cannot find myself -- find my way in these papers. Again, I don't know whether I understand you correctly. In the statement I gave in November, that I gave to you, it is stated that I came together with Milan Lukic and took away those women, or whether that statement says that that was something that I heard, that I found from other witnesses' statements. I'm still a bit unclear. I don't know exactly what it says. I'm not sure I have the right page, but I'm sure you will be able to explain this to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. There is a problem, Mr. Groome. We still don't have those in evidence. Has there been an agreement about the English version of the statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm informed that Mr. Domazet has them now. It's just waiting for his agreement to the redactions that have been made, and then it can be submitted to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: When you say redactions, is that for the purposes of witness protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I see. So that the documents that we have should be the same as that, indeed, more complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So we can go to those.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, may I suggest that if you can find the passage, if you can pick it up quickly, you take Mr. Vasiljevic to it so that we all know what it is that was said at the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, you have some papers in front of you. Is that a transcript of the -- of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's just that the papers got mixed up. So I start reading one passage and then all of a sudden there's the house at Bikovac and then the house at Pionirska Street, and then all of a sudden the hospital, because the page numbers do not follow each other. So yesterday I was thinking about the whole thing a little bit. I don't know whether I understood you correctly. I was not present when Milan Lukic took away those women. However, here I find -- I see that he took away the [redacted] [redacted], and so on and so forth. According to witness statements, I see that he took away women to be raped, that there was a woman who was three or four months pregnant.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We do not have the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I haven't finished. Then he took away her --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment, sir. Why haven't the interpreters got the statements? Surely they were given copies of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: They were given when we used them and they have been returned. We will get them a copy now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that's imperative if we're going to go through this. It's very difficult for them, especially when somebody reads, they usually speed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I can make a suggestion. It seems that Mr. Vasiljevic's copy has somehow got -- the pages are all mixed up. Perhaps we can solve this problem by furnishing Mr. Vasiljevic with a new full copy of the B/C/S version of his statement and then he would be able to review it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That would be a very good idea. But at some stage, and I don't mean now, but if you can find the passage that you think he's referring to so that you can give him at least a page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm not sure the page numbers will correspond, but if I can ask him a few questions, perhaps it we can narrow it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, we will provide you with a fresh copy of your statement in B/C/S so that there's no confusion about the pages. Can I ask you, on the copy that you have, is that from the 16th or the 17th of November?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the interview of the 16th has page numbers. However, on the 17th, I no longer have any page numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just to clarify it, the Prosecution isn't alleging that you were present when the women were taken away. We will -- I will ask you some questions about what happened in Musici in a few minutes this morning, but in case you misperceived any question that I've asked you, it's never been suggested that you took women away from Musici.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome, because I was all of a sudden afraid, because I thought that that was your interpretation, that according to your interpretation I was present, whereas I really was not. I state here that she was taken away -- what can I say. I was not an eyewitness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will try to get you a copy of that statement at the moment. We will give it to you as soon as possible. The questions that I will ask you now will not involve Musici. And I would also state that if, at any time, your recollection of what you said during your statement is different than the transcript, you are free to tell us the difference, what the difference is. I'd like to resume. Yesterday, we finished --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise once again, I don't have the list with witness pseudonyms, the two sheets of paper that I had yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Obviously, we'll need to get a few of those run off, because if the witness is not allowed to keep it, we'll need to supply him with one each day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There should be two, P164 and D22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have both copies in front of you now of the two exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the list with Prosecution witnesses, the protected ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's 164, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have a spare copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you have both of the pseudonym sheets now. When we finished yesterday, you were describing for us how, in the mornings, the van for the TO in Prelovo would pick you up at your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who actually drove that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obren Vojnovic. He used to work as a driver for the forestry, and that was the car that he had official use of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the van kept during the day?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Prelovo, unless it was away bringing or taking food. But normally it would be stationed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this van used for any other purpose other than the distribution of food? Were other units permitted to take and use this van?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was the only van we had, so it had to be there all the time. It was used for transporting food and bringing foodstuffs from the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was responsible for keeping the van at night?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was parked there in front of the command building, so the guard would have been responsible for it. It had to be there at all times. And also for other purposes, if something should happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you said in your testimony on Tuesday that you were issued a gun by the Territorial Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of the, I believe you mentioned, five different men that worked with you, were you the only person that was issued a gun?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all issued a gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you all issued guns for security reasons, to protect yourselves?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we all had to be issued with some kind of weapon. We had to have a weapon each.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what time each day would you conclude your work?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I distributed food in the evening hours, I would come back at around 10.00, if we had to drive dinner up to the positions. However, if dinner could be distributed together with the lunch, if those were only rations of food, then we wouldn't go back in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And out of the nine or ten days that you did this job, approximately how many times were you able to distribute the dinner rations at lunchtime?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened maybe once or twice. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those nine or ten days, were you ever required to stay there overnight?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no other place for us to go. We had to sleep there. Sometimes, if I had transport, I was allowed to leave, I could leave; however, I would have to be back the next morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back in Prelovo the next morning?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So out of these ten days, how many days did you actually stay overnight in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many. I may have gone home on two or three occasions. Usually, there would be no transport, because we couldn't -- we were not allowed to use the van for our private needs. The vehicle had to stay there overnight. I mean, we couldn't use it for our private business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your direct testimony -- your evidence in chief, you told us that you believe that the first person killed in the conflict in Visegrad was a Serb. What I want to ask you is, can you approximate for us when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid I might be wrong, but it would have been sometime after the release of water at the dam. On that day, maybe the day before -- no, I think it was one day after the water was let out from the dam. And, I'm sorry, and after the arrest of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would be sometime in mid-April or later; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, before, because he was killed before the Uzice Corps came, before that, before their arrival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in April or March?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April. In April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some questions about the weapons that you were in possession of in the spring and summer of 1992. Am I correct in saying that the first weapon you possessed was a Schmeisser rifle that was issued to you by the SDS political party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have a Schmeisser. I mean, I didn't take it. It's not that it was the SDS that gave it to me. I don't know how to put it. I don't know whether it was organised by the SDS via Territorial Defence. I don't know those details, nor was it possible for me to obtain this type of information. It's not that anyone told me that it was the SDS. I don't know who was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, do you admit or deny that in your statement of the 16th of November, for Defence counsel, page 30, that you said the following: "A. We were distributed these weapons in our settlement to villages, and I don't know how this was done, but I believe that it was all organised by the party; it was all done through the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who received these weapons?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody did." Do you admit you said that on the 16th of November?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But, again, it is something that I think happened. It is only my assumption. It's not something that I'm certain about. I cannot guarantee you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were most Serb men issued weapons similarly to you?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you received your Schmeisser as early as March of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time you began to travel back and forth from Prelovo, for those ten days, you were issued a different weapon, an automatic rifle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from March of 1992 until May 19th, when you were mobilised, did you carry this Schmeisser with you that you were issued?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as I told you, I exchanged it later on at Prelovo. I mean, I returned the Schmeisser and I was, in turn, issued an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The automatic rifle that you were issued, was it possible to use that gun as both a single-shot weapon and a multiple-shot weapon?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe for us how one would convert the weapon from firing a single shot to firing multiple shots?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right side of the rifle, there is a device which you use to convert the rifle for that purpose. It has to be pushed and then it's converted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you push this device on the rifle, does it make a sound?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. First you have to move the handle, I mean you have to put in the bullet, and then you use the device to set the rifle on single shots or multiple shots. First you have to put the bullet in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, would I be correct in saying that when somebody changes the rifle from one mode to another, that it makes a clicking sound; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can hear that. Yes, you can hear this click.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a weapon that is commonly called a Tommy gun or a Thompson submachine-gun? Are you familiar with the weapon I'm now referring to?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That gun has a rather unique appearance, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has a round magazine as opposed to an elongated magazine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not a round magazine. Thompson does not have a round magazine. Some Russian weapons of the similar type do, but Thompson is an English weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would agree with me that a Thompson or a Tommy gun is a unique weapon distinct from the automatic rifle that you carried; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time period, were you ever in possession of a Tommy gun?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was released from hospital, I did not have a weapon. I still had my plaster on. So I was issued with this type of weapon which was normally not issued to soldiers for combat purposes. It's not a kind of weapon that is taken by soldiers to the front line. I was given some sort of certificate and issued that weapon so that I would have something at home. But I was still on sick-leave during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say that part of your responsibility in the distribution of food in Prelovo was to ensure the security of your fellow workers?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I quite understand your question, to ensure the security. We were safe when we were at Prelovo, because we were at the command. So there was no danger present there. But when the driver and I went to distribute food, then of course in terms of security, it was expected that we would assist each other should anything happen. However, while we were at Prelovo, there was nothing I could or had to do to help them, except if they needed something from the quartermaster service. But one other thing that I should mention. We were not required to stand guard, I mean we, members of the quartermaster service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as the driver is driving the food into an area that may be dangerous, would it be fair to say that you would be accompanying him, you would have your automatic rifle, and you would be alert to any dangers that might face you and the driver; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He would have a rifle too like myself, so we would both have rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on these trips from Prelovo to Visegrad to collect foodstuffs, would the van pass through Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If going from Prelovo to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we would pass the villages of Kurtalici, Musici, and Sase, and Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that as the driver was driving, you were in possession of your automatic rifle, again to ensure the security of the van and both of you?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How shall I put it? We both had a weapon and of course we carried it for our own safety. But on the road from Prelovo to Visegrad, we never had any problems. But should anyone open fire on us on that journey, it would be very difficult for us to protect ourselves. But I never had any -- I never experienced any trouble, any problems from Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But am I correct in thinking that you kept possession of your rifle at all times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I would hold it like this on my knees. Sometimes it would be next to me, next to the seat of the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can you describe that? Because it was impossible to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe, using words, exactly how you would hold your weapon in the van. You made a --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended. Sometimes I would be holding it in my lap; sometimes it would be next to my seat, not far from me, of course, so that I could grab it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you motioned with your hand down to the right side of your knee. Is that where you would keep it when --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to my seat, yes. Yes, next to my right knee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it would have been considered a very serious breach if you had ever lost that weapon, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described on your direct testimony that the place that you worked out of in the Prelovo area was, I believe you first said, a school and then in a house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the places that you worked, there was no place for you to safely lock up your weapon and leave it; am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say because of the weapons. We prepared meals there. Troops were there. So it was advisable to get away from there so that other soldiers wouldn't get in our way as we prepared food, so that nobody would interfere with our work. It wasn't for the sake of weapons, it was for the sake of the kitchen itself, to better organise ourselves, to prepare food easier. We were not far from the school. We were about 200 metres down, perhaps, on the road itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is, the places that you worked, there was no safe place where you could lock up your gun for the night, was there? You had to keep it with you at all times.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, one always had the rifle with one, even when sleeping. But nobody would take your rifle from you. But perhaps it did happen now and then, but no, not as a rule. Everybody had his own rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never lost your weapon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the nights that you were able to go down to your home near Visegrad, you would take that rifle with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I went from Prelovo home?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Overnight? No, I carried the weapon with me, of course. I couldn't leave it find.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your commander at this time was a person by the name of [redacted] [redacted]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Prelovo, no. Krsta Papic was the commander in Prelovo. [redacted] was in Visegrad. I don't know what he was. He was up there, but he wasn't the Commander-in-Chief. I do not really know what his position was. In Prelovo, it was Krsta Papic who was my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, sorry, if you want to object, do make yourself orally known, otherwise you'll have to stand forever. What is the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Groome has just mentioned a name which is on Mr. Vasiljevic's list, so could we have it struck out from the transcript, please. It is line 16 --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- from Mr. Vasiljevic's list. If that could be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. I'm just trying to see where number 16 has been mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's VGD16, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, right. I'm sorry. Yes, I see it. Yes, that will be redacted. Thank you for drawing it to our attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, other than VGD16 and this person you've told us is named Papic, did you have any other superiors during this time that you were in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We at the quartermasters, we didn't. Now, as for the companies, I suppose soldiers there in those companies, they must have had those. But we down at the quartermasters, and we were five, no, we didn't. And then a battalion is then subdivided into companies and they each have their own commanders and whatnot, but we were not under them. They were around villages, standing guard there. They couldn't issue orders to us. Our duty was to supply them with food. But apart from that, they could not issue any orders to us because we were not under them, we did not belong to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that you were released from the Uzamnica gaol on the 1st of June, the day your cousin was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that that is the day that you were released?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think it was the 1st.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it have been the 2nd?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know. The 1st, the 2nd, don't know. Could be. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was either on the day that your cousin --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Let me try to explain it. They told me that. Now, perhaps they told me on the 2nd that he had got killed. He was killed on the 1st, but perhaps they did tell me on the 2nd. Now, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question in another way. Approximately how many days transpired between the day you got out of gaol and the day you attended your cousin's funeral?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He and two of his neighbours were killed, or rather the two of them were from Gornja Vardiste, and he came from Donja Vardiste. But they did not pull the bodies out immediately. I know that they got out one of those other two first, and the two of them were buried before my cousin. The Defence has the document issued by the church, saying it was the 7th. So it was five days in between. So he was brought home on the 6th, or perhaps on the 4th, because he was first taken to the hospital in Visegrad, and they dressed him. I can't really tell you exactly. I know that he was first taken to the Visegrad hospital, to the morgue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, I'm more interested in whether you remember being at your home a number of days between the time you were released from gaol and the time that you attended the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there was some time in between. But, now, how many days? I mean, they knew that he was killed, the command, but they simply couldn't get his body out, because he was killed on the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to estimate for us how many nights you spent in your own home before you attended the funeral of your cousin?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would make four days, or what? Thereabouts. Because I also went to Vardiste before the funeral to see my uncle, before he was brought over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to now move to what occurred in the village of Musici. You were here and heard Witnesses VG55 and VG59 describe what occurred in the village of Musici the night that they saw you. Was their account essentially correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, sorry, that day when I was there, that only day when I stopped the car up there -- now, what should I say? I do not know about the theft of his money in his house. The man says so, so it must be true. But I was only by his house. And when those stole his money and searched his house, I mean, he has no reason to make it all up. But I don't know that and I don't think he'd tell me about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to be clear, they never testified that you were present when Milan Lukic returned two or three days later and committed other crimes against them; they never said that you were there on that second time, did they?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, at least that's how I understood them, yes, although that witness, 059, he said, "I didn't see him, but I guess he was there," or "I assume he was there."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go to the first night, the first event that they talked about in Musici, the day that you were in Musici, and ask you, did this happen during the time that you were working at Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see Milan Lukic and his men for the first time on that day?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had finished lunch. We took the pots and all the crockery back down, and I had then to take the dry pack. And I wanted to go and get a bath. I stood on the road. They were coming from the direction of Zupa, and I lifted my finger. They stopped and took me. So perhaps about a kilometre before Musici, he said, "I'm going to see here if there are any weapons around," because allegedly somebody had fired shots at their police patrol. "So what have you got to do with it? He didn't fire at you," or something. But he then stopped in the village, and above the house -- no, above -- no, in front of Vila Uzeir, and he was moving fast, he walked fast always, and he entered the house --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, I want to ask you some more specific questions about where it was that you first saw them. Let me ask you this: This day, do you recall if this is one of the days that you were able to distribute the evening rations early in the day, or was it one of the days that you had to serve the dinner in the field?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said that that day we distributed lunch, and for the evening meal, the dry pack was in order, so there was nothing that we had to carry there in the evening. I mean, they had some tins, dry pack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did you finish your work on that day?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could have -- I returned perhaps at around 4.00, half past four.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you on the road with your finger up looking for a ride? Were you in Prelovo itself?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right next to the kitchen, because the kitchen is by the road, I mean the building, next to a walnut tree. There's a big walnut tree there, and right next to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you first saw Milan Lukic, he was in a car; correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was driving the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there more than one car in the group?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of those cars the red Passat that we spoke about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the car that Milan Lukic was driving.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else in that -- who else was in that car with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a fair-haired woman, quite young, perhaps 20, 20-something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With him, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the other cars, or can you describe the second car that you saw in that group?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether it was a Lada or what now. I'm not sure. I don't know. I mean, I put my finger up and stopped him, and he was the first one in that column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody in the second car in the group?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: VGD4, as he was stepping out at Musici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anybody else in that car with VGD4?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I mean, there were five or six of them, or maybe even seven or eight. I don't know. I don't really have the best recollection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The third car, do you recall recognising anybody in that car?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was a man, rather obese, who could be 25 or something, but I don't know what his name was. I'd seen him around. I saw him in Milan's company, but he wasn't there when I returned from the hospital. I don't know his name or anything. All I know is that he was overweight. And as far as I know, he had a beard, but I can't really tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got into the red Passat, am I correct in saying that you sat next to Milan Lukic, in the front seat?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was behind him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anybody in the back seat with you?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This person you've described as a fair-haired woman, had you ever seen her before?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was not from Visegrad. She was not a Visegradian, that I'm sure about. But I used to see her again around there prior to my going to the hospital, but I don't know, I think she came from Serbia. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic armed at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he dressed in a uniform that you described to us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was always in that same uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there anything lying about inside the car which would have indicated to you that perhaps they had been engaged in some criminal activity such as stealing property or other criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean whether there was something on the seats in the car? In the car? I didn't see anything in the car. Whether there was something in the boot, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how far did the car drive after it picked you up, before it stopped in Musici?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not much. Three, maybe four kilometres, if that many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Milan Lukic's car the first of the three to pull over in Musici?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the other two cars stop as well?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior -- excuse me. You travelled this road just about every day in the course of your work, and my question to you is did any of your superiors, or had you heard from any official source that somebody had been fired upon as they drove past the village of Musici? Had you been given any official warning of that nature?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that Milan Lukic said he wanted to stop to search for weapons because a police patrol had been fired upon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He never said to you that he wanted to harass these people or to commit any crimes against these people, did he?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't, no. Well, it was three kilometres; that is, we travelled together for three or four kilometres, and all I said was, "What have you got to do with it? He didn't fire at you. So why don't you let them solve it." But the man that he is, I don't know, he stopped, went into the house to those [redacted] oh, I've just mentioned their name, sorry. He entered the house belonging to the father of Witness VGD59, and I followed. I asked them to leave those people alone. Well, if he went to look for weapons, then let him look for weapons. So he went in and they said, "No, no, we have nothing," and then he said, "Well, let's have all the people from the village together." So that VG59 went, and he was about to search the attic, the loft, and -- the attic. And I asked the brother, 055 - as a matter of fact, we went to school together, we were school fellows - I asked him, "Have you got anything up there?" and he said, "No." And so I said, "Milan, let these people go. I know them."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is, can you tell us exactly what you said to Milan Lukic when he first says he wants to stop at Musici? Did you say to him, "Please, Milan, take it easy"?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Don't do something to them." Well, I think had I said anything bad, he would have reacted just as badly, the man that he was. But I didn't. I simply asked him nicely, and then I think he looked for weapons. He didn't look for money or for valuables. He did not hit anyone that day. What happened later, well, that ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said, "Don't do something to them." Did you also say, "Don't provoke these people"?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Something. Something. I can't really tell you word for word what I said. But I didn't say anything to provoke him into doing something bad. I mean, I didn't say anything as if I'd wanted to do something wrong. I even said, "Well, I trust every word this man says. I know they are honest people," and I said I knew the man well. I was very ill at ease because his father used to work with my wife. I mean, he was an elderly man. He was a craftsman and a good man. So what do I know? So, of course, I mean, but there was fear present and all that. But he looked for weapons. He didn't take any gold, he didn't look or ask for any money, not that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said, "Please don't provoke these people," what kinds of things would have been a provocation? What were you asking him not to do to these people?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to mistreat them, not to harass them, to stop shouting and yelling so that people wouldn't be so afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you worried about the safety of these people?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, frankly speaking, it never occurred to me that he would open fire. It's just that I didn't want him to harass them or mistreat them in any way. Well, he didn't open fire. Thank God he didn't shoot. But he kept asking him, begging him. I was standing next to the door and I know that he did not ask for any money or gold on that day. He didn't hit anyone. And then he was quiet, he wasn't really shouting around the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Tuesday you told us that you were aware that two of the men in the house were police reservists, and that you did not tell Milan Lukic this fact. Why did you not tell Milan Lukic that these two men were connected with the police?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you understood me correctly. VG55 and his brother were members of the reserve police force, that's what I wanted to say. They were members of the reserve police force before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you told us on Tuesday that you made the intentional decision not to tell Milan Lukic that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, I would have never told him that, because I know that then he would have searched them, he would ask for weapons. And, no, it never occurred to me to tell him that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he's already there searching them for weapons. What else do you think he might have done to these two men if he learnt that they were members of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He most probably would have mistreated those people. He would go on searching for weapons. He would never give up. I don't know what else he would have done. But he would for sure insist on finding the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that the first time that you believed Milan Lukic and his men were dangerous was on the 7th of June. My question to you is why did you believe at this stage that Milan Lukic presented a danger to these men because they were police reservists? What did you base that on?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you did not believe that these men were dangerous until you saw them kill people on the 7th of June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never in my life was I present at a killing incident up until that time, until the 7th of July. I had never prior to that eyewitnessed anything nor heard any such thing. And then when I was able to observe it personally, when I was able to see for myself how rude, how heartless and merciless he was, then of course ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the incident we are talking about now is more than one week before you witnessed that, and yet you felt that these two men who were police reservists were in some type of danger in the company of Milan Lukic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand. Are you referring to Prosecution witnesses or the two men whom I just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I think you have to put it together. You're fragmenting your question a little bit. You mean he was aware at the time that if Milan Lukic knew they were police reservists, then they were in some form of danger from him, that's what you're after.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's the two men that Mr. Vasiljevic has referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, put it all together in one question, because I think it is difficult for the witness if you don't put it all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First I am referring to VG55 and his brother who are police reservists, those are the two people I'm referring to, and I'm asking you, at that time, the day you were in Musici, you were aware that these men were in danger or faced some danger from Milan Lukic if he knew -- if he knew that they were police reservists; correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is why? What did you know about Milan Lukic and his men on this day that made you believe that?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's like this: You see, if he had found weapons on him, he would have mistreated him. I would have only created the situation very difficult for me if I had told them they were members of the reserve police force, that they had weapons for sure. He would have never stopped until he found something. I never thought about that. I could -- I think I even guaranteed that I -- that [redacted] could be trusted, that he was with me in school, and the fact that he was a member of the reserve police force was not surprising because there were many such cases, not only them. The police force was still mixed. I didn't consider it to be any violation of the rules. It just didn't seem strange at all. There were many Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point in time, had you heard of Milan Lukic and his men having mistreated other people, at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up there in the village?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any place in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 20th of July or the 27th of July, I don't know. What I heard later on throughout those three or four years is another matter. It's difficult for me to tell you whether, on the 27th, I had heard that he had mistreated someone. It's very difficult for me to be precise. I don't think that he caused any serious incidents prior to the 27th. Well, according to the statements, I can now see that he killed this woman, Bahija Zukic. But I didn't hear about that before the 27th. I don't know exactly when I heard about that. Nor did I ever hear about the incident in Pionirska Street until I arrived here in The Hague. Before that, I had never heard of such thing happening, never, never. I did for Bikovac but not for this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, when you arrived in Musici, you went directly to the home of VG59; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, sorry. It was the house of his father. And VG59 was living with his wife. He was building a house in the village of Musici. Actually, he completed the house. And it was his brother who lived with his father. And Witness 55 also lived with his father. So it would have been his brother and 055 that lived with his father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you went to the front of the house but you did not enter it.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't enter the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't want to enter the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't want to, because it was all too embarrassing for me. I wish he didn't stop by the house, or I wish I'd stayed in the car. I only -- I'm glad that on that occasion he didn't commit any such thing, that he didn't threaten people or loot the house or hit anyone. He didn't do anything bad on that day, and I'm glad about that, because I was there. He was looking for weapons, and I could see that he was entering various rooms inside the house. He probably had some suspicions. He probably thought that someone was hiding up there. I think he made up the story about the shooting incident involving the police. It was just a pretext for him to enter the house and search the premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you armed when you were standing in front of that house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With your automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away was the car parked from the house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not more than 20 metres away. Twenty, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, according to you, you tried to set the family at ease by telling them that they need not worry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said to [redacted], again, I told you that we went to school together, and I mean thank God nothing happened on that day, thank God he didn't do anything on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you said, "Don't worry. It's all right."

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, it never occurred to me that he would open fire. I didn't simply think that it was possible, that he would kill someone or Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. something. But I was worried because, you know, every time there's a search, people are afraid. But I didn't think that he was about to do something bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say to them, "It's all right" in order to keep them calm? Is that the reason why you told them, "It's all right," to keep these people calm?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, so that they wouldn't be afraid. I just told them, "Just don't worry. He will conduct his search and everything will be over soon," because he wasn't looking for anything else other than weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was your belief that if these people did remain calm, it was less likely that the situation would have escalated and somebody would have gotten hurt; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How shall I put it? I didn't want those people to be afraid while he was conducting his search. He was actually on his own, I mean he was acting on his own. There was no way for me to order him anything. If I had been at the wheel of the car, I would not have stopped, I would not have let him go search the house. But I never drove a car. And if, again, I would have been at the wheel of the car, there would have been no way for him to say, "Stop here for awhile until I search this house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But am I right in saying that you told him to be calm in order that they would just comply with what Milan Lukic was doing, searching their home, and by doing that there was less chance that they would be hurt by him; is that correct? Is that what you were thinking?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I'm correct, you probably want to say that if they had reacted in a different way, that he would have opened fire, that they protested in a way -- I mean, had they behaved differently that he would have acted differently, is that what you're trying to say? I mean, it's possible. Maybe if those people didn't want to let him in, well, it's possible -- actually, I'm sure that he would have reacted differently, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would have behaved differently, I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they did resist, if they did try to fight back against Milan Lukic, do you believe that he would have shot some of those people?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, I didn't believe that he would shoot, but I wasn't sure what he could do. It was all a long time ago, you know. I offered some guarantees. I said, "I trust these people." I said, "[redacted], don't fear. I do believe what you're saying." I didn't say to [redacted], "Let him search the house."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, I think you have referred to that person now three times. Just be careful. He is one of those protected witnesses, is he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, what I'm getting at is, it was your belief at that time, if this family remained calm and just permitted Milan Lukic to search the house for weapons, then nobody would get hurt; wasn't that your belief at that time?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- how shall I put it? It's not that it was my wish. I didn't want him to search that house and those people. I just wanted to -- the whole thing to be over as soon as possible, without any problems. It was my wish to see the whole thing finish as soon as possible. I wanted to go home. It's difficult for me to describe this to you. I didn't have any intentions whatsoever, sir. I didn't insist on anything. And I believe that one of the witnesses stated, but not before the Chamber, that I had told his brother that I could guarantee about him, that I knew that he was an honourable man, something to that effect. I think that it was VG59 who stated that to the investigator, something to that effect, that I offered some guarantees. And I cannot quote what he said, but it was about some guarantees that I offered in respect of his brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vasiljevic, you've just told us that it was your belief that if the people remained calm, it would all be over with and there would be no problem. What I'm asking you now is, is that why you told the people it would be all right, to make them calm, to make them less afraid? Is that why you said it would be all right?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at this time, you've just testified, you had some concerns about their safety. You were worried about them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was embarrassed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I would be correct in saying that these people in this house, they would have been entitled to be worried as well. That would have been a reasonable response to what was happening, to be worried, to be afraid; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and that's exactly what I wanted to tell them. And then there's another thing that I'd like to say. I passed by that house every day while going about my business, and it was not in my interest. But when I was with him as we were coming from Prelovo, I wanted to guarantee for this family because I knew them and I knew the brother and I knew that he was honest and sincere, and I also knew their father. But if I had told him that they were members of the reserve police force, he would have behaved differently. He would have searched the whole property including the barns and outside buildings, and so on and so forth. I didn't want to tell him that, though I knew perfectly well that they were members of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, isn't it a fact that on this occasion you told these people not to worry, it will be all right, that you told them a lie in order to get them to comply with what Milan Lukic was doing in their house. Didn't you lie to them in order to get them not to resist Milan Lukic? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never told them not to resist. I just wanted to tell them not to be afraid, that everything would be all right. I don't know how to explain this to you. I didn't have any bad intentions. It was not my desire to see them harassed or mistreated by him. I didn't want him to provoke these people, to shout at these people, and I just wanted him to leave the house as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VG55, you have known this person for a very long time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You both are around the same age and essentially grew up together; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't grow up together. Our two villages are far apart. [redacted] [redacted]. So I did know him as a child for about two years, and then later on we got together again and I can say that I knew him maybe from 1967.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any reason that you know of that VG55 would have come before this Tribunal and said something that was false about you? Do you know any reason they would do something like that?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that he would have ever appeared before this court if Lukic hadn't done what he did. If I had been alone in his house, I don't think that he would have ever come here, despite the fact that I was maybe in uniform or armed, because my intentions would have been different. But I don't think that he's charging me that much here. I mean, I was at his house. And he also said that he believes that I was there on the second or the third day when Lukic came but that he didn't see me. It was just his assumption. Maybe he saw him at the time of the arrest, that I was in the car. But that's not something that he said. It's just that my name was mentioned in connection with a very bad person who committed crimes, and many witnesses appeared and testified to that effect. I don't wish to repeat everything they said; I would be wasting your time. 115, for example, I had two fractures during the period of two years, and she apparently never saw me on crutches. I mean --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, what I'm asking you is you and VG55 never had any kind of dispute or anything happen between you two that would make him want to say something false about; correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We were even very good friends. His brother, VG55, his wife worked not very far from where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, if VG55 did want to get you in trouble or say something false about you, he could have said that he saw you on the second night when the really bad things happened in Musici; correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, see, sir, now that I'm thinking about this whole thing, I think that I would also be angry if someone came to my house carrying a weapon. When I look at it realistically, of course I understand that it was altogether very embarrassing and that people did not feel at ease. But I was simply there with Lukic. I didn't act badly in any way. I didn't encourage Lukic to do anything bad, and I didn't tell him anything bad about VG55 and others. If I had spoken badly about them, I'm sure that Lukic, the kind of man he was, would have -- no, no, I didn't. I understand, I understand their feelings, but it's just that at that time, it didn't occur to me. My intentions were the best possible intentions. And I had problems with alcohol and, you know, but -- and then this house at Bikovac, in Pionirska Street, never, sir. Never did it occur to me to point a rifle at any man. But I am here being held accountable because I was in the company of a bad person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VG59, you have known VG59 for a very long time as well.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he's the wife of the brother, 55. Our villages are next to each other. I went to her village to school. She's somewhat younger than I.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no reason that you're aware of that VG59 would say anything false about you, is there?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, that's exactly what I'm trying to say. Of course, the witnesses didn't enjoy the situation, I mean the fact that I was there, but I feel thankful because they could have said all kinds of things about me, that I had come there on the second or third occasion, that I had taken those women to be raped, and so on and so forth. I think that they were rather correct in their testimonies. And the fact that I was there with Lukic on that particular day, I can only offer my apologies. I'm glad that at least on that day nothing bad happened. I was naive a little bit, and I was under the influence. Milan's mother, Milan's father begged me. But in the house of VG55, if I wasn't able to help, I don't think -- who would? If I had spoken badly about him, I think this whole situation would have ended up differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Should we pause here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Before we go, though, Mr. Groome, we've now got the application for safe conduct for the Defence witnesses. Have you got any objection to safe conduct being granted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would like to see the application, Your Honour, before I offer my opinion to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We're usually the last to get these things. We got ours yesterday. Would you have a look and see if you can find it and let us know, because I'd like to have it dealt with before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, over the break, the interpreters have expressed some of their concerns regarding they had some difficulty translating your answers this morning. May I ask if it's possible to answer my question with a yes or no, do that, and let us know if you need to explain it further. And if you do explain your answers, please do it a little more slowly and try to speak in complete sentences, and it will be of assistance to the interpreters. You told us that Mr. Lukic searched the house for weapons. Did they, in fact, find any weapons?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Milan Lukic asked to check the attic of that house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that point in time, didn't you then ask one of the people in that house if he had any weapons in the attic?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, whether there were any weapons or something. The brother of VG55, whether there was anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was you that had asked him, not Milan Lukic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. Milan, how shall I say it, perhaps I was afraid, so I asked him, "Well, have you got any?" I said that he was my school fellow. "No, I've got nothing, Mitar." Had he made a sign to me to show that he had it, then I'd go with him surely. So I said to Milan, "Milan, I believe every word this man says," so as to stop Milan from going to the attic. And had he indicated to me somehow that he did have some, then I would have gone with the brother of 55. And had I gone up there and returned, I would have nonetheless said that there was nothing there. But I didn't want to say anything, and I guaranteed then that he was telling the truth, the brother of Witness 55. So he didn't go to the attic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. And had I kept silent, Lukic would have gone to the attic, I'm quite sure he would have done that had I not had this idea. And for that [redacted] I apologise, Your Honours, I mentioned again the name of this witness. But I again said, forestalling Lukic, I said him, "Do you have any?" and he said "No, I don't." And then I said, "Milan, I trust every word this man says." I simply wanted to get away from the house as soon as possible. I felt very awkward being there, because after all, we went to school together. We've known each other for years. We would stop, meet, have a coffee or something. Or when we would both be going to work, we would meet in the street and talk, never any bad intentions. And I'm very happy that nothing bad happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, my point is that when you told Milan Lukic that, "I've asked for weapons, he says no, I guarantee it," Milan Lukic believes you; is that correct? He does not go up to the attic.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've heard VG55 describe Milan Lukic's group and yourself as storming the house, rushing towards the house. When they approached the house, did they rush to the house, did they storm the house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you meant. Are you asking me if I entered the house, that Witness 55 said that I entered the house, is that it, or 59? Is that what you are asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I can see where the source of this confusion is. If you keep referring him to other witness' evidence, you are in effect asking him to keep in mind the evidence. Why don't you just ask him, did they storm the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, when the group arrived at the house, did they rush into the house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean abruptly, that we were running towards it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Well, why? I mean, it's 20 metres. It's 20 metres off the road, the house is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they walked up to the house; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait. No, no. This house, VG -- that is, the father's, it's straight up there, 20 metres away, and those other houses are to the right. Now, how did they go there? There's a lane there and there is woods there and there are plum trees and orchards, but I can't tell you how they went there because I don't know, because there's -- the road forks off and there are trees. And whether they ran up to those houses, I don't know. I couldn't see that. One couldn't see that from the house belonging to Witness 59 father's house. I don't think that I could see that because they went to the right. At some point, they stopped their cars and then you follow for ten minutes -- ten metres more, and then there is a road which forks off to that locality. And his house is the first one from Prelovo, above the road, and below the road is Uzeir's house, his neighbour. But they went to the right, and I don't think I would have been able to see them, seeing the house that I was in, because it's rather steep there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, I'm just asking you about the house that you yourself went to. Was it just you and Milan Lukic that went to that house, or were there other men?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the three of you go to that particular house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from that car, from the car driven by Lukic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Lukic and the woman walk to the house or run to the house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not running. It's less than 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this woman armed?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they get to the front door of the house, is the door open or is it shut?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I don't know. Lukic, Lukic was leading. But I think it was open. I think. I was the last one to get there. I think it was open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he stop at the doorway and wait for the owner of the house to come and invite him in, or did he just walk into the house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was talking with a brother, 59. No, this one didn't try to prevent him from entering. I didn't see any trouble there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he simply walked into the house, he wasn't invited into the house.

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he did not use force. He did not force his way in. I think that there was one of those in the doorway, but I can't really bring this scene back to describe it properly. I don't think that anyone tried to stop him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in the first session this morning that, looking back on the events of that evening, you do not believe that Milan Lukic was really looking for weapons. My question to you is, looking back on it, what do you believe the intent of Milan Lukic and his group was on that evening in Musici?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what was the intent? I think he was looking for weapons. No, I think he would have been happy to have found any weapons, because that would have given him a pretext. But I don't know. I saw all sorts of things in the statements. I was never present when he looted, and they did all sorts of things, getting money and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VG59 testified that you told them that they were looking for someone named Avdo who had allegedly killed a Serb woman and her two children. Do you recall ever saying anything like that to VG59?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't. Did he say before the Court that I had said that? Is that how it was, that I had said that or that I had asked that? Is that what he said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quoting from the transcript at page 658, VG59 stated: "He," referring to you, "told us that they were looking for a certain Avdo who had killed a Serb woman and two children, and that they were searching the houses to arrest him, and I believed him." My question is did you ever say anything about an Avdo to that witness?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm asking you again, does he say that I asked him or Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, you have had read to you what he said. Now, that's clear enough. That's to describe to you the reason for the question. The question is simply did you ever say anything to VG59 about a person called Avdo on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nor do I know anything about the killing of a Serb woman and two children. I'm not aware of a Serb woman with two children being killed. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasiljevic, you also said on Tuesday that the people from the village gathered together, and Mr. Domazet asked you, and I'm quoting from the transcript at page 44: "If I understood you well, you said that a little later some other villagers of Musici also turned up; is that correct?" And you said, "It is." My question to you is did these people voluntarily come and gather in one spot? Was that what you were saying on Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think VG55, I believe, went to tell them to come to the house of 59's father, villagers I mean. That is what Lukic had demanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is correct is that these people did not voluntary gather, Milan Lukic demanded that they be rounded up together so that he could say something to them; correct?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, VG55 also told us that Milan Lukic said two things. The first thing was that they weren't to go anywhere, they were to remain in that village. Do you recall Milan Lukic saying that to these people?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I was outside, I was outside in front of the house, but I believe he said that. They were inside. But I do believe he did say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second thing that he allegedly said to them was, he told them that they would be safe there. Do you recall Milan Lukic saying that to the group of people from Musici, that they would be safe in their village?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you that I was outside. And whether he said that, well, he must have. But he was talking to those people while inside the house so I couldn't really overhear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at the doorway of that house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the house, not far from the door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people had been gathered into that house?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, 15, 20. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you left Musici, did you get into the red Passat again?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Milan Lukic and this fair-haired woman in the Passat as well?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anybody else in the Passat?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see anything in the Passat that led you to believe that Milan Lukic or this woman had taken anything from these people?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the fair-haired woman and Milan Lukic say anything to each other regarding what had happened in Musici?

utterances.speaker: MITAR VASILJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall what they were talking about. I'm not really sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
